scope: Priority actual-photo evidence cross-check and exact Hays same-specimen diagnostic requirements; nonpublishing, no key admission.
previous_contact_sheet_visual_review: All 317 reduced-resolution Hays source photo tiles were visually reviewed in batches completed by PR #120, which was still open when this source triage began.
source_limitations: Historical source licenses from private attributions.json, mostly CC BY-NC; exact live photo source remains blocked and publication under CC BY-NC requires noncommercial-rights and photo ID check.
Archive contact-sheet actual pixels support only explicitly described visible traits, NOT 1-mm floral measurements, same-rootstock proof or formal herbarium accession authentication.
Species and source-photo labels represent iNaturalist Hays research-grade records; that is evidence of an observation, not settled taxonomic occurrence nor county nativity under BONAP.
Full-resolution iNaturalist source URLs and direct AWS image download were tried; browser rejects exact observation/photo links and container network DNS unavailable.

Generic diagnostic microscope key drawn from regional-independent published literature; published Florida/Hawaii/Australian accounts are supplementary, not overriding Diggs/Hagenbuch for Texas character interpretation.
Specimen source rights, public gallery photo rights and scoring admission are kept separate. No publishing rights approved, no scored shard/UI/manifest changed.

specimen_gate_records.name: Aegilops cylindrica
confirmed_at_contact_sheet_resolution: Jointed slender cylindrical flowering spike, with separated mature spike-axis pieces photographed against a person's palm.
Separate photo set shows basal leafy tuft and leaf collar.
not_observable: Internal number of fertile florets inside a specific detached joint; thick asymmetrical ribbed glumes and their awns at 1-mm scale.
Exact 2015/1999/FNA floret-unit terminology reconciliation, independent Hays voucher and nonplanted habitat status.
diagnostic_references: Diggs et al. (1999), p.1235: sessile, 2–5-flowered spikelets on jointed axis; awned glumes.
UT PRC Williamson County Aegilops cylindrica: rachis joint with closely fitted one spikelet, asymmetrical awned glumes with 5–7 ribs, terminal spikelet often different.
FNA via Burke: 3–5 florets, 2–3 fertile; source ranges and counting scopes should not be treated as contradictions without dissecting.
Avoid false comparison with awnless Rottboellia/Mnesithea jointtails and wheat.
specimen_gate_records.next_action: Re-access high-resolution original IDs 682960212 and 682960258; dissect a ripe segmented spikelet in millimeter photo under expert review and verify Hays site identity.

specimen_gate_records.name: Bothriochloa bladhii
confirmed_at_contact_sheet_resolution: Dark purple slender flowering racemes held against fingers, and distinct long-hairy culm node ring.
Sheath-collar is present in source images.
not_observable: Translucent median channel along torn-apart rachis internode and pedicel; requires high magnification.
Glume pit varies and can be absent in some sessile spikelets; neither pit presence nor absence should be a single strict species filter.
Distinguishing same Hays planted/wild stand from Dichanthium aristatum.
diagnostic_references: Hawaii key Faccenda (2023, printed p.99): groove on dried pedicel usually requires ~20–40×; could be violet/purple not truly clear.
POWO GrassBase Bothriochloa bladhii: flattened pedicels with medial translucent line; pitted lower glumes may be absent.
Regional source hierarchy remains Hagenbuch/Lemke vegetative when treated and Diggs reproductive when treated, FNA/GrassBase secondary.
specimen_gate_records.next_action: Collect a single dried Hays inflorescence, separate a pedicellate spikelet by its base and use 20–40× scope to image BOTH faces of the median groove plus a paired spikelet.

specimen_gate_records.name: Dichanthium aristatum
confirmed_at_contact_sheet_resolution: Red-purple digitate racemes with individual spikelet-like units, and a bright leaf junction/collar view.
Some hand-held closeups likely have enough original image pixels for detailed spikelet-pair outline.
not_observable: Reliable *absence* of a translucent pedicel and rachis medial line must be established by examination, not by lack of visible line in a thumbnail.
Glume/rachis and lower florets to differentiate other local Dichanthium and Bothriochloa.
Hays site planting-origin status.
diagnostic_references: AusGrass Dichanthium aristatum: pedicels lack translucent medial line.
Faccenda (2023) hawaiian combined genus key recommends microscopic torn pedicel inspection, and warns line may be difficult to see in full-color fresh photos.
specimen_gate_records.next_action: From a dried Hays specimen, microdissect pedicel and rachis at 20–40×, show absence of median groove on BOTH sides while independently confirming species spikelet/glume structure.

specimen_gate_records.name: Stapfochloa ciliata
confirmed_at_contact_sheet_resolution: Curving, sometimes looped, one-sided radiating racemes are present.
One original photograph includes a ruler adjacent to a flowering branch and another shows culm/collar.
not_observable: One fertile plus two sterile florets in isolated spikelet with fertile lemma ciliate midvein and margins.
Exact ~1.8–2.8-mm fertile lemma and 0.9–2.7-mm principal awn lengths and comparator differences against S. canterae.
Hays BONAP county nativity on actual source map and a Hays local voucher.
diagnostic_references: POWO GrassBase under Chloris ciliata, now accepted Stapfochloa ciliata: 1 fertile floret, 2 sterile; fertile lemma 1.8–2.8 mm; lemma margins and midvein ciliate.
Faccenda/other southern flora generic key, only corroborating regions.
specimen_gate_records.next_action: Dissect a mature attached spikelet into one fertile and two sterile florets; measure each lemma and awn and record under 10–40×, compare with voucher-verified S. canterae.

specimen_gate_records.name: Stapfochloa canterae
confirmed_at_contact_sheet_resolution: Bent curved one-sided racemes against measuring tape, a detailed hairy culm node/collar, and isolated spikelets on a ruler.
The separate pieces appear adequate as a starting source for microscope retake requests.
not_observable: Species-specific sterile floret length/shape and awn differences against S. ciliata, with published diagnostic key for canterae.
Exact identity of the original Minnette Marr specimen independent of original iNaturalist label.
Introduced planted/escaped status; current NC license check.
diagnostic_references: Kew accepts Stapfochloa canterae and records Texas introduced; older Chloris canterae synonym.
Published modern key directly contrasting canterae with ciliata and original Hays microscope verification still missing.
specimen_gate_records.next_action: Use existing Hays specimen from observation 137935400 if available: remove one mature spikelet, measure fertile/sterile floret stack and lemma ciliation next to a voucher S. ciliata spikelet, have grass specialist sign off.

specimen_gate_records.name: Tridens congestus
confirmed_at_contact_sheet_resolution: Dense pinkish or pale tan spikelet-bearing head and multiple individual flower-bearing spikelets seen beside a hand.
Bunchgrass-like vegetative base and overall culm context.
not_observable: A single isolated 3-veined mature lemma showing shallow notch, tiny midvein extension and characteristic hairs under backlight.
Basal short node-compressed rhizome linked to flowering stem; distinguish from other Tridens.
Published deep-cleft vs short-notch terminology reconciled by specimen.
diagnostic_references: Diggs et al. 1999 p.1330 species treatment calls a cleft lemma tip.
UT PRC Williamson County Tridens congestus has mature lemma notch up to ~0.2 mm and central vein projection 0.3–0.5 mm, with very short crowded-noded rhizomes.
Kew GrassBase reports rhizomes and ciliate membrane; actual rhizome visibility is not a filter requirement.
specimen_gate_records.next_action: Dissect one mature lemma, backlight the notch and mucro under 20× with scale, show basal rhizome from the exact same Hays individual.

specimen_gate_records.name: Pappophorum bicolor
confirmed_at_contact_sheet_resolution: Feathery flowering panicles and tufted dry-grassland habit are present; photographed individual flowering units show many awns.
not_observable: 11–15 lemma appendages from ONE lemma and actual lemma body length separated from spikelet.
P. mucronulatum also has 11–15 awns per lemma; cannot hard-code awn number as bicolor-exclusive.
No independent Hays voucher or original pixel closeup of 3–4 mm lemma vs 2–3 mm of comparator.
diagnostic_references: Kew GrassBase accounts for P. bicolor and P. mucronulatum share 11–15 awns, sometimes overlapping lemma lengths; assess multiple characters.
specimen_gate_records.next_action: Photograph a separated mature fertile lemma body with 0.1-mm scale and all appendages, compare side-by-side with voucher P. mucronulatum, and document same plant's whole panicle.

specimen_gate_records.name: Echinochloa walteri
confirmed_at_contact_sheet_resolution: Awned branched flowering heads and distinctly papilla-based sheath hairs are visibly documented in the Hays source set.
Several different original observations contribute wet-habitat context.
not_observable: Attached mature spikelet body length, lemma apex and specific awn insertion distinguishing E. crus-galli/E. muricata.
Hair presence is typical but rare less hairy E. walteri can occur, so hard presence or visible awn threshold excludes legitimate examples.
No botanically expert Hays photo signoff or public-source rights clearance.
diagnostic_references: FNA and Go Botany Echinochloa accounts: papillose sheath hairs useful but not individually exclusive; awn and mature lemma structure varies.
specimen_gate_records.next_action: Use original photos of actual Hays source to measure two ripe spikelets and their lower lemmas plus papilla-based sheath hairs at same-specimen scale.

specimen_gate_records.name: Melica nitens
confirmed_at_contact_sheet_resolution: Several Hays source views clearly depict nodding oatlike spikelets, foliage and flowering clumps.
Historical 2015 Hill Country Appendix B cites Dingee 89 (SWT) from Hays County.
not_observable: Original published voucher sheet for Dingee 89 has not been examined; separate photograph panels may represent different individual plants.
Fully mature basal crown growth (source calls hard subrhizomatous base rather than true long rhizomes), opened ligule and sterile terminal floret.
Photographic identity of this year's local observation is not established by 2015 voucher alone.
diagnostic_references: Hagenbuch & Lemke 2015 Hill Country vegetative key and Appendix B Dingee 89 (SWT) Hays gathering.
Diggs 1999 regional Melica nitens flowering morphology; older rhizomatous vs subrhizomatous descriptions require nonexclusive wording.
specimen_gate_records.next_action: Find image/data of Dingee 89 SWT in TORCH or university herbarium; compare its ripe spikelet, short basal growth and actual Hays iNaturalist source ID 282514813.

specimen_gate_records.name: Rottboellia campestris
confirmed_at_contact_sheet_resolution: Very slender jointed, nearly awnless cylindrical seedheads; one photographed against a hand and one field-grown clump.
2015 Hays County Appendix B has two published historic gatherings: Carr 10681, Sanders 4100 (TEX-LL).
Hays photo ID 684707043 is historically marked CC0, with observed source link and archived attribution metadata.
not_observable: Actual original Carr/Sanders TEX-LL herbarium sheet features/pitted glume not independently measured.
Embedded sessile fertile and pedicelled sterile spikelets, pitted lower glume and rachis niche are not visible on current contact-sheet size.
Exact CC0 license and source/photo species label have not been reverified live; image not yet approved for site.
diagnostic_references: Diggs et al. 1999 printed p.1258 under Coelorachis cylindrica: slender disarticulating rachis with pitted fertile sessile glume and companion reduced pedicelled spikelet.
Hagenbuch & Lemke 2015 Appendix B: two published Hays vouchers; modern Kew preferred Rottboellia campestris and ITIS alternative Mnesithea cylindrica.
USDA GRIN synonyms Coelorachis and Mnesithea.
specimen_gate_records.next_action: Ask photo owner to verify exact CC0 status and label for Hays photo 684707043 as general photo, and target original TEX-LL sheets Carr 10681 and Sanders 4100 for pitted glume/rachis dissection and expert ID.
